answers.text: The reply puts the fixes in priority order and says what needs a person
answers.evidence: The reply orders the work by severity: 'Fix first: these break reservations' (items 1-5, to fix before launch), then 'Fix next', then 'Smaller issues', with a 'Suggested order'. It names what it could not check ('I didn't run VoiceOver or TalkBack ... so the screen-reader points come from reading the markup') and leaves 'one pass on a real iPhone with VoiceOver and larger text turned on' to a person.

mapping.title: Basket hold expires after 10 minutes with no warning and no recovery
mapping.reason: The basket never shows the 10-minute hold, and after it lapses Continue says 'Something went wrong. Try again.' with no way forward. That is D10's untimed hold and misleading error; the review adds that retrying never works because the timer is not reset.

mapping.title: Pick-up day and pick-up session are not reconciled and can disagree
mapping.reason: The day is chosen on the tool page and the session in the basket with no check between them. The review's run ends with the drill 'pick up Saturday 17 October' against the 'Wednesday 21 October' session, and the desk can't tell which is right. That is D15, down to the same example.

mapping.title: Calendar accepts closed days; refused only on the confirm page with no link back
mapping.reason: 'Every date can be chosen, including days the library is closed'. The confirm page later says 'The library is closed on Friday 16 October…' and gives no link back to change the day. That is D06.

mapping.title: Days and sessions before the tool's available-from date are accepted
mapping.reason: The calendar allows 'days before the tool is back', the basket accepted the 10 Oct session for a pressure washer available from 17 Oct, and the fix is to offer only sessions on or after each tool's available-from date. That is D14.

mapping.title: Double tap on Confirm creates two reservations
mapping.reason: The Confirm button stays enabled with no busy sign for 1.5 s, and tapping it twice gave FT-4471 and FT-4472 for the same drill. That is D12.

mapping.title: Basket not emptied after a confirmed booking
mapping.reason: After confirming, the header still showed 'Basket (1)' on the confirmation page. That is D18's basket left full after 'Reservation confirmed'.

mapping.title: Truncated tool names hide the difference between the two drills on phones
mapping.reason: Names are cut to one line with an ellipsis, so at 375 px both drills read 'Cordless drill 18 V, co…'. That is D03.

mapping.title: A search with no matches silently keeps the old list
mapping.reason: A search for 'hammer' still shows all 10 tools with no message and no screen-reader announcement. That is D02's no-match search with an empty status region.

mapping.title: Dark-mode 'Available from' badge fails text contrast
mapping.reason: The badge is #2f7d4a on #1d2622, 3.07:1 for 16 px bold text, failing 1.4.3. That is D04 exactly.

mapping.title: Dark-mode calendar day borders and selected-day fill are faint
mapping.reason: In the dark theme the review measures the calendar's day outlines at 1.6:1 and the selected-day fill at 1.2:1. Both are below the 3:1 that WCAG 1.4.11 asks for component boundaries and states, and the selection rests mostly on a 2 px border, so a member choosing a pick-up day in dark mode on a phone gets a weak cue for which day is selected. No ground-truth defect covers the calendar's non-text contrast.

mapping.title: Loan-length dropdown shadow invisible in dark mode
mapping.reason: A drop shadow that doesn't show on a dark background is cosmetic. The review gives no measurement and no harm, such as the open list blending into the page; the dropdown's real faults are R15.

mapping.title: On phones search sits below all ten tools behind an icon-only filters button
mapping.reason: Below 480 px the search form moves under the results, the filters button has no visible word, and the CSS order rules make keyboard order disagree with visual order. That is all D01. The review places the focus mismatch on desktop rather than on phones, but the cause and the fix (drop the order rules) are the same.

mapping.title: Basket pick-up sessions shown in reverse order
mapping.reason: row-reverse with wrap-reverse shows Wed 28 Oct first and Sat 10 Oct last, while keyboard and screen-reader order follows the dates. That is D11.

mapping.title: Membership and mobile fields reject normal formats
mapping.reason: 'ft-01234', 'FT 01234', '+44 7700 900123' and '07700 900 123' are rejected with no normalising. That is D17.

mapping.title: Loan-length custom dropdown traps the keyboard and can't be dismissed
mapping.reason: While the list is open, Tab cycles through the options and Escape does not close it. That is D09's keyboard trap. 'Tapping outside doesn't close it either' is the same missing dismissal on the same control, and the native-select fix covers both.

mapping.title: Fixed 'Reserve this tool' bar covers the footer
mapping.reason: The footer with the desk phone number sits under the fixed bar even when scrolled to the bottom, because nothing pads the page clear of it. That is D08's phone case.

mapping.title: 'Added to your basket' message is brief, with no next step
mapping.reason: The message disappears after 1.2 s, and the only lasting way on is the 'Basket (1)' link at the top: brief feedback with nothing lasting nearby, which is D07. The item does not say the member wrongly believes the tool is reserved, so it is not D26.

mapping.title: Tool grid scrolls sideways at 320 px
mapping.reason: minmax(330px, 1fr) gives 346 px of content in 320 px, so the page scrolls sideways (1.4.10). That is D05.

mapping.title: Confirm-page 'Change' link drops the chosen session
mapping.reason: The 'Change' link goes to the basket without the current session ticked. That is D13.

mapping.title: Returning to the confirm page clears the typed details
mapping.reason: Coming back to the confirm page clears the details the member already typed. That is D22.

mapping.title: Three-tools-per-member limit not enforced in the basket
mapping.reason: The basket does not enforce the three-tool rule. That is D21.

mapping.title: Done page reads the tool name twice to screen readers
mapping.reason: A hidden #c-tool copy makes the tool name read twice. The review uses 'confirmation page' for the done page throughout (it is also where it saw 'Basket (1)' after confirming), so this is D24.

mapping.title: 'Choose a pick-up session' error link points at a non-focusable container
mapping.reason: Following the error link does not put keyboard or screen-reader members on the session radios, so they have to hunt for the field the error is about. Many members will hit this error because the basket starts with no session selected. Not in the ground truth: D19 is the tool page's day message, and D23 is the duplicated date entry.

mapping.title: No 'Skip to content' link
mapping.reason: The review shows no long repeated block to bypass (the only header element it mentions is the 'Basket (1)' link). It does not say landmarks or headings are missing, either of which meets WCAG 2.4.1, so this is a generic checklist remark with no harm to these members shown.
